keystore.title: Keystore
keystore.subtitle: Named passwords that encrypt private keys. Every key below names the one that wraps it.

summary.ownerless: no owner, can never be encrypted: {count}
summary.noKeys: This account owns no private keys yet.

credentials.heading: Credentials
credentials.empty: No credential yet. Until one exists, new private keys cannot be stored encrypted.
credentials.name: Name
credentials.deleteBody: Only an empty credential can be deleted; the wrapping key is what makes its private keys readable.
credentials.defaultHint: New private keys are encrypted with the default credential unless a request names another.
credentials.unlockBody: Enter this credential's password. It is not stored anywhere, and there is no recovery if it is lost.

rotate.title: Change the password of “{name}”
rotate.help: Only the wrapping changes: the private keys themselves are not re-encrypted.

assign.title: Encrypt “{name}” with a credential
assign.body: The key is decrypted with whatever holds it now and re-encrypted with the credential you pick. Nothing is copied.
assign.label: Credential

hint.locked: A locked credential still protects its keys; open it before signing or exporting them.
hint.plaintext: Cleartext keys stay readable without any password. Encrypt them with a credential.
